questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: Identify the standard for territorial claims under effective occupation
questions.stem: Case 1: Observer 1 asks whether a treaty without courts or police can establish sovereignty under effective occupation.

options.text: Requires actual administration and control on the ground
Confuses occupation with earlier discovery claims

options.text: Treats a signed treaty as proof of occupation
options.misconception: treats a signed treaty as proof of control

options.text: Assumes naval presence alone satisfies occupation

questions.explanation: The correct option identifies effective control on the ground; treaties, flags, or naval presence alone did not establish sovereignty under the Berlin standard.

questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.topic: Boycott after the partition of Bengal
questions.learningObjective: Explain the aim of the Bengal boycott
questions.stem: Case 4: Observer 4 describes students refusing British cloth after 1905; what was the immediate aim of the swadeshi boycott?

answer.exemplar: The swadeshi boycott aimed to revive Indian industries and foster national pride by refusing British goods, especially cloth, after the partition of Bengal.

questions.topic: Land crowding and secret oaths in Kenya
questions.learningObjective: Connect Kenya land loss to anticolonial resistance

options.text: Links land loss and oaths to anticolonial movement
Treats oaths as mere criminal conspiracy

options.text: Blames only missionary activity alone
options.misconception: blames only missionary activity alone

options.text: Sees land loss as voluntary land sale
options.misconception: sees land loss as voluntary land sale

questions.explanation: Land loss and secret oaths fueled organized resistance; treating them as crime or missionary effects understates the grievance.
questions.hint: Land loss and oaths fed anticolonial resistance.
